sections.heading: Section 1: Work Done by Constant & Inclined Forces

questions.q: A force of 60 N pulls a box across a horizontal floor through a distance of 8 m. The force acts at an angle of $60^\circ$ above the horizontal. Find the work done by the force.
A crate of mass 15 kg is lifted vertically at a constant speed through a height of 4 m. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, what is the work done against gravity?
A box is pushed 5 m along a horizontal floor against a constant frictional resistance of 35 N. What is the work done against friction?
Calculate the kinetic energy of an athlete of mass 70 kg running at a speed of 8 m/s.
A rollercoaster car of mass 500 kg starts from rest at the top of a frictionless hill of height 20 m. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, find its speed at the bottom of the hill.
A bullet of mass 0.02 kg traveling at 300 m/s penetrates a wooden block to a depth of 0.15 m before stopping. What is the average resistive force exerted by the wood?
A skier of mass 60 kg starts from rest at the top of a slope 30 m high. When reaching the bottom, her speed is 20 m/s. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, how much energy was lost due to friction?
questions.answer: Initial potential energy $E_p = mgh = 60(10)(30) = 18000\text{ J}$. Final kinetic energy $E_k = \frac{1}{2}(60)(400) = 12000\text{ J}$. Energy lost $= 18000 - 12000 = 6000\text{ J}$.

questions.q: A package of mass 4 kg slides down a rough incline of length 10 m and vertical drop 6 m. If the resistive force is a constant 8 N, find the speed of the package at the bottom (starting from rest, $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$).
questions.answer: Work done by gravity $= mgh = 4(10)(6) = 240\text{ J}$. Work against friction $= 8 \times 10 = 80\text{ J}$. Net kinetic energy $= 240 - 80 = 160\text{ J}$. $\frac{1}{2}(4)v^2 = 160 \Rightarrow 2v^2 = 160 \Rightarrow v^2 = 80 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{80} \approx 8.94\text{ m/s}$.

questions.q: A particle is projected up a rough incline ($30^\circ$) with initial speed 10 m/s. If $\mu = 0.2$ and $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, how far up the plane does the particle travel before coming to rest?
questions.answer: Deceleration up slope: $a = g(\sin 30^\circ + \mu\cos 30^\circ) = 10(0.5 + 0.2 \times 0.866) = 10(0.5 + 0.1732) = 6.732\text{ m/s}^2$. Distance $s = u^2/(2a) = 100/(2 \times 6.732) \approx 7.43\text{ m}$.

sections.heading: Section 4: Power and Vehicles in Motion

questions.q: A car of mass 1200 kg travels along a level road at a constant speed of 30 m/s. The engine is working at 45 kW. What is the total resistance to motion?
questions.answer: $P = Fv \Rightarrow 45000 = F(30) \Rightarrow F = 1500\text{ N}$. Since speed is constant, driving force equals resistance: $R = 1500\text{ N}$.

questions.q: The same car (mass 1200 kg, engine working at 45 kW) faces the same resistance of 1500 N while traveling at 20 m/s. What is its acceleration at this instant?
questions.answer: Driving force at $20\text{ m/s}$: $F = P/v = 45000/20 = 2250\text{ N}$. Net force $= 2250 - 1500 = 750\text{ N}$. Acceleration $a = 750/1200 = 0.625\text{ m/s}^2$.

questions.q: A truck of mass 5000 kg ascends an incline of 1 in 20 ($\sin\alpha = 1/20$) at a steady speed of 15 m/s. The engine power is 60 kW. Taking $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, find the resistance to motion.
questions.answer: Driving force $F = P/v = 60000/15 = 4000\text{ N}$. Gravity component along slope $= mg\sin\alpha = 5000(10)(1/20) = 2500\text{ N}$. At steady speed: $F = mg\sin\alpha + R \Rightarrow 4000 = 2500 + R \Rightarrow R = 1500\text{ N}$.
